catalog_locator: Saved file. Tone system: p. 92, §1.2.4.2.3 'Le système tonal', Tableau 48 'Système tonal du lekaniŋi (F. Evouna Ntoutoume, 2003, p.23)'. Author's own group-B60 tonal summary: p. 108. Accent hypothesis for B60-70: p. 272, §3.1.3, with the validation caveat at p. 273.
catalog_quote: Sur le plan paradigmatique, on relève un système de deux tonèmes ponctuels en lekaningi: un tonème haut (H) et un tonème bas (B). [...] Sur le plan syntagmatique, les unités suprasegmentales inventoriées en phonétique ne sont que la combinaison de ses deux tons de base. De manière générale, le ton montant correspond au tonème Haut et le ton descendant est relié au tonème Bas. || (printed p. 108, group B60 summary:) Sur l’axe paradigmatique, l’analyse tonologique fait apparaître un tonème haut (H) et un tonème bas (B) admis dans l’ensemble des parlers du groupe B60. Les tons modulés appartiennent au domaine phonétique. || (printed p. 272, on groups B60-70:) Le calcul des fréquences montre clairement que, le dualisme tonale a été abandonné en position T1 et n’est plus observable qu’en position T2. [...] Les faits tels qu’observés laissent soupçonner une évolution vers un processus accentuel et confirmer l’intuition de certains auteurs (G. Philippson, 1991; E. Dodo-Bounguendza, 2010), qui ont envisagé que les parlers de la zone B semblent laisser coexister deux systèmes prosodiques, à savoir le système de tonalité à côté de l’émergence de phénomènes accentuels.

new_statements.translation: On the paradigmatic level one finds a system of two punctual tonemes in Lekaningi: a high toneme (H) and a low toneme (L). [...] On the syntagmatic level, the suprasegmental units inventoried in the phonetics are only combinations of these two basic tones. In general the rising tone corresponds to the High toneme and the falling tone is linked to the Low toneme. || (p. 272, on B60-70 as a group:) The facts as observed lead one to suspect an evolution toward an accentual process and confirm the intuition of certain authors (Philippson 1991; Dodo-Bounguendza 2010), who envisaged that the zone B varieties seem to let two prosodic systems coexist, namely the tone system alongside the emergence of accentual phenomena.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Lekaningi is described as a two-tone language (H vs L tonemes; rising and falling are H+L combinations). No word-stress placement is stated anywhere for Lekaningi. The only accent remark is the author's own group-level diachronic observation that in B60-70 (Lembaama, Lindumu, Lekaningi, Latéghé, Lintsitsèkè) the H/L contrast in disyllabic stems is neutralised in the first stem syllable (T1) and survives in T2, which he reads as an incipient accentual process coexisting with tone; no position for that accent is given.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Lekaningi. The accent remark is a hypothesis flagged by the author as needing detailed synchronic tone studies of other zone-B languages to validate (p. 272-273).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation-form lexical items (387-word questionnaire, Evouna Ntoutoume; 140-word comparative list, Niama Niama; consultant Apouba Germaine, b. 1980, Boumango = southern variety). Tone described at the word/stem level; the accent remark concerns disyllabic stem tone patterns across the B60-70 groups, not a specific word-stress rule.
new_statements.identity_note: The saved description covers Lekaningi Sud (data from Moupia south of Franceville for Evouna Ntoutoume; consultant from Boumango for Niama Niama). Niama Niama (p. 87) notes two main dialects, Nord (surrounded by Lembaama B62) and Sud (per DDL/Van der Veen 2014), and (p. 35) that Lekaningi is sometimes treated as a dialect of Lembaama (B62, mber1257) or a variety of Lindumu (B63, ndum1239); Bastin et al. 1999 code it 'B64', Maho B602. Glottolog kani1279 has no dialect entries.

sources.note: Section 1.2.4 Lekaningi (B602), printed pp. 87-93: phonology taken over from Evouna Ntoutoume (2003); two punctual tonemes H and B, rising/falling tones are combinations (p. 92); no mention of stress or accent for Lekaningi. Author's own diachronic tone chapter (p. 272, 283, 297) says that in groups B60-70 the H/B contrast is neutralised in T1 and kept only in T2, and suspects 'une évolution vers un processus accentuel' coexisting with tone; no placement rule.
